clue.text: First year student in access to further education

indicators.note: in tells us the student is placed inside the word for access

parts.note: recourse is access to a source of help
a fresher is a university student in their first year

explanation.surface: A first-year undergraduate gets into further education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; the student word splits the access word in two. A fresher is British slang for a first-year undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is extra training that brings old knowledge up to date, a kind of further education.

clue.text: Element of Antony's setback around 8

indicators.note: around says the battle's name is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: Mark Antony was defeated at the naval battle of Actium in 31 BC
the answer to 8 down abbreviates to NI

explanation.surface: Something basic in Antony's defeat involves a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts NI, the usual abbreviation of 8 down, inside ACTIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinium is a radioactive chemical element, number 89.

clue.text: Brood putting a foot between partners

indicators.note: between places the foot in the middle of the two partners

parts.note: S and N, South and North, are partners at the bridge table
a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: Someone producing offspring sets a foot between two partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North and South play as partners, giving S and N either side of PAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn, like brood, is the offspring produced at once by a creature.

clue.text: DIY twice collapsed all over capital

indicators.note: collapsed suggests the letters of these words have fallen into a new heap

explanation.surface: A do-it-yourself job has fallen down twice all over town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges the letters of DIY TWICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Citywide describes something spread throughout a city, such as a capital.

clue.text: Time an offender may be held as such …

indicators.note: an offender breaks the rules, here the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A criminal serving time might be kept in that role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offender' rearranges TIME AN; the ellipsis carries on into 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a person held in a prison or other institution.

clue.text: … his plight could be a warning to others

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might become something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A prisoner's plight might serve as a warning to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HIS PLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored vessel carrying a beacon to warn other ships of danger.

clue.text: Artist has risen from wilderness

indicators.note: risen in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ARA is Associate of the Royal Academy, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter has climbed up out of the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risen' reverses ARAHAS, as a down entry read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the great African desert, a vast wilderness.

clue.text: Part of the UK maybe found even in India

definitions.text: Part of the UK maybe found even in India

parts.words: Part of the UK maybe found even in India
parts.note: the even letters of India, its second and fourth, are N and I, the usual abbreviation for this part of the UK

explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like 'even so' but asks for the even-numbered letters of 'India'.
explanation.definitionFit: This province is one of the four parts of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Expect no one but one may appear

indicators.note: may appear suggests the letters could show up in another form

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Don't count on anyone, though one might turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear' rearranges EXPECT NO with I.
explanation.definitionFit: An exception is the one left out, as in 'all but one'.

clue.text: Operatic princess finds house in America

parts.note: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

explanation.surface: A princess from opera finds a home in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; 'in America' defines a state found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, a place found in America.

clue.text: Its share was life-threatening for the Snark

definitions.text: Its share was life-threatening for the Snark

parts.words: Its share was life-threatening for the Snark
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's Hunting of the Snark the hunters threaten its life with a share in a train company

explanation.walkthrough: 'share' here is a stock-market holding, not a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's poem lists a share in a train company among the hunters' weapons against the Snark.

clue.text: Counter to what could be art

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of the preceding word may be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with what someone thinks counts as art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a noun (a shop counter) but is the preposition-like definition, as in 'counter to expectations'.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart is an old word meaning across or in opposition to, so counter to.

clue.text: Rotation is constant between poles

indicators.note: between puts the constant in the middle of the two poles

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: Turning motion is steady between the ends of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: PI sits inside S and N, the poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is rotation, as of a ball or planet turning on its axis.

clue.text: Flight for flight?

parts.note: a flight of stairs built for flight, that is escape, from a burning building

explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is an outside staircase used to flee a building on fire.

clue.text: Gordius could be put up as my name for wages in work

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the assembled letters are read upwards
in puts the payments inside the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
dues are payments owed, wages

explanation.surface: The setter might be known by this name for his pay at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns the whole assembly upwards, as a down entry. Gordius is the setter's own pen name, so the clue refers to itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordius is the pen name of this puzzle's setter, so an example of an assumed name.

clue.text: All together at seamen's assembly

indicators.note: assembly suggests the letters of the sailors' word are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Sailors gather in one body for their meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges SEAMENS.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for in a body, all together.

clue.text: Become stubborn if force is held by weapon

indicators.note: is held by puts IF and F inside the weapon

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Someone grows obstinate if a gun is pointed at them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War, a crossword staple for 'weapon'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen is to become rigid, figuratively to harden one's resolve.

clue.text: A little cunning about this, perhaps

indicators.note: about says the cunning word goes round the other piece

parts.note: sly means cunning
this clue is an example of a light, a crossword entry

explanation.surface: A crafty move around this one, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: A light is an entry in a crossword grid, and this clue is one; SLY wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, a little.

clue.text: Ruffians contrive amusements

indicators.note: contrive suggests the letters are devised into a new form

explanation.surface: Thugs organise some entertainments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrive' rearranges RUFFIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Funfairs are fairs with rides and sideshows, places of amusement.

clue.text: Firm run badly: work in intelligence organisation, where there's plenty

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: badly says the letters of run are jumbled
in places the work inside the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A badly run company does work for the spies, in a land of plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about a business, but splits into three pieces; 'badly' scrambles only the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia is the horn of plenty, a source of abundance.

clue.text: Alien with music track pioneer

parts.note: rock is a kind of music
ET is the film extraterrestrial, an alien

explanation.surface: An alien teams up with a musician on a pioneering track.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephenson's Rocket of 1829 was an early railway locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's Rocket was a pioneering steam locomotive on the railway track.

clue.text: There's nothing stupid in Denmark

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
dense means stupid

explanation.surface: Nobody in Denmark is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Denmark' defines a city found there; 'There's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is Denmark's third city, a place found in that country.

clue.text: Called back to growl

indicators.note: back says the word for called is read in reverse

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A phone call returned with a snarl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RANG.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnar is an old word for snarl or growl.

clue.text: She's one in alternative setting

definitions.note: the 's is a link meaning 'is', leaving 'She' as the definition

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the alternative

parts.note: else means otherwise, an alternative
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: She is someone in a different setting.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside ELSE; 'setting' is part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, so a female, a she.

clue.text: No clues are designed to be open

indicators.note: are designed suggests these letters are built into a new shape

explanation.surface: A puzzle with no clues is meant to be open-ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are designed' rearranges NO CLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclose is an old verb meaning to open.

clue.text: Room occupied by old bag

indicators.note: occupied by puts the old piece inside the room

parts.note: a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A room is taken over by an old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' in the surface is British slang for an unpleasant old woman, so the room seems occupied by her; it is in fact the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag.

clue.text: Poor-sounding record

indicators.note: sounding tells us the answer is said like the letters of a disc

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record

explanation.surface: A badly recorded disc.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEDY is said like CD.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby and run-down, poor in condition.

clue.text: One in fix has to persevere

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the word for fix

parts.note: to solder is to fix metal together
one is the Roman numeral I
to can mean on, as in pulling the door to

explanation.surface: A man in a tight spot has to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'to' giving ON is a loose equivalence, as in 'set to' meaning 'set on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to persist doggedly despite difficulty.
